title: Tesla Is Investing Aggressively in its Next Generation Technology | TSLA Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc downgrades Tesla back to a SELL, reversing the HOLD stance he adopted when the shares fell to $300 earlier in 2026, where he closed his puts and short position for a profit. At about $379 (stated), the stock trades on 175x forward earnings against his $113 DCF fair value — roughly 70% downside over 12–18 months — and he says he is tempted to buy put options again, more so near $400. His base case rests on a weak third quarter: revenue flat at $28 billion year on year, EPS down 44%, automotive revenue down 3% to $20.5 billion, energy revenue down 16%, and operating income down 56%; he raised near-term DCF estimates only because 2026 capital spending was cut from $25 billion to $20 billion. The bull points he concedes are real: Full Self-Driving subscriptions up 67% to 1.74 million at about $99 a month, services and other revenue up to $4.6 billion, Tesla Semi volume production started, four new European FSD approvals, and about 1,000 robotaxis testing in Austin. The bear case is valuation and competition: the price assumes robotaxis and robots are inevitable, Chinese EV makers are eroding share in every contested region, and EV volumes have likely peaked near two million a year.

calls.bear_case: Valuation prices robotaxis/robots as inevitable: 175x forward earnings is ~6x the S&P 500, ~40x the average carmaker and ~6x big-cap AI names. Chinese EV competition is eroding share in every contested region, EV volumes likely peaked near 2m a year, and any investor realisation that timelines slip could mean ~70% downside.
